1. Heard Mr. Ashutosh Kane, the learned counsel for the Applicant/ Plaintiff.
KAVITA SUSHIL JADHAV
2. The Plaintiff seeks to move without notice for the reasons set out in paragraph 28 of the Plaint.

I find that there are sufficient 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L)
24983.2025.doc averments and disclosures made in the Plaint to sustain the ex-parte application for ad-interim reliefs.

3. The Plaintiff has filed the present suit and interim application seeking injunction restraining the Defendant from committing disparagement by making false, misleading and disparaging representations and scandalous statements / representations against the Plaintiff's goods sold under the trade mark/ name PITAMBARI and/ or by carrying out unfair trade practices in the form of Pitambari Products Private Limited vs Sawariya Collection Delhi on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122493715/
1 advertisements, online/ digital commercial and marketing activities by using the Plaintiff's PITAMBARI trade mark/ name.

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted that the Plaintiff is one of the most trusted companies in the fields/ segments of food, homecare, healthcare, perfumery, agriculture, cosmetics, etc. in India and abroad.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff is using various distinctive trade marks in respect of its various products used in a variety of industries to distinguish its goods/ products from others as well as inter se.

It is submitted that one such inherently distinctive and well-known trade mark honestly and independently adopted by the Plaintiff's predecessors in the year 1983 is "PITAMBARI" in respect of its homecare segment.

It is submitted that during the relevant time, the Plaintiff's predecessors in title applied for and secured registrations of the trade mark "PITAMBARI" in English and various other Indian vernacular languages under the provisions of the Trade Marks Act.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has also applied for and secured registrations of trade mark labels inter-alia containing the word 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc PITAMBARI as their leading,
prominent, memorable and essential feature under the provisions of the Trade Marks Act.

A list containing the details about the Plaintiff's registered trade marks and the registration certificates along with the renewal certificates are annexed to the Plaint and marked as Exhibits "A" and "B-1" to "B-36"
to the Plaint, respectively.
It is submitted that the said registrations have been renewed and are valid and subsisting.
It is submitted that the Plaintiff is now the registered proprietor of all the above mentioned trade marks.
The details pertaining to the chain of title from the Plaintiff's predecessors to the Plaintiff are given in paragraphs 5 to 9 of the plaint.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff's trading/ corporate name also contains the trade mark PITAMBARI as its memorable, prominent,
leading and essential feature.
It is submitted that the Plaintiff is in short known as PITAMBARI.

5. It is submitted that since its adoption, the Plaintiff has been openly, widely, continuously and extensively using the said trade mark/ name in relation to the said products and services and has made large, ready and ever-increasing sales of the goods/ products/ services under the said trade mark/ name.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has also taken efforts to popularize the goods/
products and services under the said trade mark/ name and has spent large sums of money on publicity, advertisement and sales promotional activities in respect thereof.
The Plaintiff's sales figures running in several crores and expenditure on promotional activities have been tabulated in paragraph 12 of the plaint.

A copy of the certificate of the Plaintiff's Chartered Accountant certifying the correctness of the 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc aforesaid figures is annexed to the Plaint and marked as Exhibit "C".
The Plaintiff has also annexed specimen invoices in respect of sales of its products under the said trade mark/ name PITAMBARI at Exhibits "D-1" to "D-13"to the Plaint.
Copies of specimen of the Plaintiff's promotional and advertisement material bearing the said trade mark/ name are annexed to the Plaint at Exhibit "E".

It is submitted that the Plaintiff and its Managing Director Mr. Ravindra Vaman Prabhudesai are recipients of several prestigious awards and accolades which are enlisted in paragraph 12 of the Plaint.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has a huge social media presence on Facebook, Instagram, Youtube, LinkedIn and Pitambari Products Private Limited vs Sawariya Collection Delhi on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122493715/
2 X (formerly known as Twitter).

sentences.text:
Exhibits "F-1" to "F-4"
to the Plaint contain relevant extracts from the said social media websites.
It is further submitted that the Plaintiff is operating a domain name/ website www.pitambari.com since 2000.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has obtained registration of the said domain name pitambari.com on April 11, 2000 and thereafter,
of pitambari.in on August 22, 2014 and pitambari.co.in on February 02, 2016.
6.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff has been vigilant in safeguarding and protecting its statutory and common law rights in the said trade mark and name PITAMBARI and has initiated legal action before this Court against third parties attempting to misappropriate or misuse the same.

It is submitted that this Court, in Interim Application (L). No. 20800 of 2025 filed in Commercial IP Suit (L) No. 20770 of 2025 by the Plaintiff, has prima facie recognized the goodwill and statutory and common law rights of the 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc Plaintiff in the said trade mark and name PITAMBARI and has restrained the Defendants in the aforesaid suit from infringing the Plaintiff's registered trade mark PITAMBARI and passing off.

A copy of the ex-parte ad-interim order dated 14 th July, 2025, passed by this Court in the abovementioned Interim Application has been annexed to the Plaint at Exhibit "G".
7.

It is submitted that the Plaintiff's PITAMBARI product has received appropriate approvals under the relevant statutes, and is manufactured and sold under appropriate licenses and complies with all necessary legal requirements.
It is submitted that the Plaintiff's said product has also undergone various tests with regard to its efficacy and safety, keeping in mind the interest and preference of the consumers.

8. According to the Plaintiff, in or about July, 2025, it came across the video uploaded by the Defendant on its Instagram page and Youtube Channel (Youtube Shorts) which was posted on 2 nd July, 2025.

It is submitted in a span of 47 seconds, it has been portrayed by the Defendant's representative that: (a) the Plaintiff's said product (PITAMBARI powder) can be used for cleaning other things but consumers should stop using the same for cleaning articles of worship [Laddu Gopal (God's Idol)]; (b) Consumption of the said product may have hazardous health effects as the said product contains chemicals which are harmful to human consumption; and (c) If consumers themselves cannot consume such chemical substances (Pitambari Powder), how can they subject their God [Laddoo Gopal 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc (God's idol)] to the same?

A soft copy of the Impugned Video and transcription of the same (along with English translation) are annexed to the Plaint and marked as Exhibit "H-1" (in pen-drive) and Exhibit "H-2"
respectively.

It is submitted that the Impugned Video, which was uploaded on Instagram on 2nd July, 2025, has garnered massive viewership of over 2,45,000 views and has received over 6,455 likes and over 181 comments within a short span of 1 month (as on 5th August, 2025).

Further, the Impugned Video has been shared over 6,700 times on Instagram alone (as on 5th August, 2025).
9.

Mr. Kane, on behalf of the Plaintiff, submits that the Defendant has deliberately, consciously and maliciously made, published and circulated the Impugned Video with an intention to slander,
denigrate and disparage the Plaintiff's said product.

He submits that the Defendant has made/
Pitambari Products Private Limited vs Sawariya Collection Delhi on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122493715/
3 published misleading statements and insinuations with regard to the Plaintiff's said product by projecting that it contains hazardous chemicals unfit for cleaning articles of worship and of a quality inferior to the other product thereby seeking to convey a clear unambiguous message that the Plaintiff's said product should not be used.

sentences.text: He submits that the Plaintiff's said product has been denigrated by the Impugned Video of the Defendant and has been equated with hazardous chemicals and shown in poor light with direct reference to the Plaintiff's said PITAMBARI product.

10. It is submitted that not only the Impugned Video but even the storyline, content and message conveyed by the Impugned Video is 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc not permissible in law.
It is submitted that the intent of the Impugned Video is clear, i.e., to mislead and discourage the consuming public from using the Plaintiff's said product qua articles of worship.

Similarly, the viewership of the Impugned Video on the Defendant's Instagram profile and Youtube channel makes it amply clear that the Impugned Video showing the Plaintiff's said PITAMBARI product in a bad light, has reached the public at large and is amounting to denigration of the Plaintiff's said product.

It is submitted that the storyline and message sought to be delivered by the Impugned Video is that the Plaintiff's said product contains chemicals which are unsafe for human consumption and that the products which humans cannot use, should not be used to clean articles of worship (idols of Gods).
It is submitted that this storyline is clearly flawed as it is inappropriate to expect copper and brass vessel cleaning preparations to contain edible/ consumable ingredients.
It is submitted that the mala fides of the Defendant are writ large as the Defendant is specifically degrading the Plaintiff's said product.

It is submitted that the content, intent and message conveyed by the Impugned Video is wrong and false and only with a view to cause irreparable injury, harm,
loss and damage to the Plaintiff and the goodwill and reputation acquired by it in the said trade mark and name PITAMBARI and the said product thereunder, by misleading the consumers.

11. Mr. Kane submits that the Impugned Video taken as a whole and the entire storyline, manner of depiction, intent and message conveyed by it has the effect of seriously debasing and tarnishing the 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc image of the Plaintiff's said product and is a malicious attempt to erode the equity, goodwill and reptation of the Plaintiff's said product.

It is submitted that the use of the Impugned Video by the Defendant is wrongful, illegal, fraudulent,
reckless and malicious.
Mr. Kane has placed reliance on Gujarat Coop. Milk Marketing Federation Ltd. v. Hindustan Unilever Ltd. , [2018 SCC OnLine Bom 7265];

12. It is submitted that the illegal acts committed by the Defendant of denigrating and damaging the reputation and goodwill of the Plaintiff, have occurred within the jurisdiction of this Court in that the Impugned Video is freely accessible online on the internet and/ or is being telecasted/
broadcasted and is available/ easily accessible and can be viewed in Mumbai.

In the circumstances,
the injury, loss, damage and disparagement that has been caused to the Plaintiff and its said product by virtue of the Impugned Video, is caused inter-alia in Mumbai and hence, the cause of action has arisen within the jurisdiction of this Court.

It is submitted that in view thereof, and under the Pitambari Products Private Limited vs Sawariya Collection Delhi on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122493715/
4 provisions of Section 20 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908, this Court has jurisdiction to entertain and try this suit for disparagement of the Plaintiffs said product.

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions advanced on behalf of the Plaintiff and have perused the material on record.

The same prima facie indicates that the Plaintiff's trade mark and name PITAMBARI has acquired a very high level of goodwill and reputation on account of open, extensive and continuous use thereof for the past more than 40 years.

The Plaintiff has secured registrations of the said trade mark and name PITAMBARI not only in English but also in different vernacular languages, that too in relation to a wide variety of goods and services.

The Plaintiff, under its name and trade mark PITAMBARI, is said to be engaged in various segments such as home care, health care, agriculture, food care, agarbatti, pooja, perfumery division and agro tourism.

The annual sales turnover figures produced by the Plaintiff in respect of the said trade mark and name PITAMBARI for the year 2023-2024 run into hundreds of crores of rupees and the Plaintiff is said to have spent almost 17.5 crores of rupees in sales promotional activities, for the said year.
The aforesaid facts prima facie support the Plaintiff's argument that its said trade mark and name PITAMBARI is well-known.
14. Before considering the factual matrix, it would be appropriate to consider the jurisprudence qua disparagement and denigration of goods.

It is a settled law that a tradesman can call his goods to be the best in the world or that his products are better from those of others, however, while doing so he cannot directly or indirectly state that goods of its competitors are bad on inferior.

Further, for making out a case for disparagement, three integers are relevant- (1) intent of the content; (2)
manner of the content and (3) storyline of the content 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L)
24983.2025.doc and the massage sought to be conveyed by it.
In my opinion, Mr. Kane's reliance on Hindustan Unilever Vs. Abbott Laboratories (Supra) and Ceat Limited Vs. Apollo Tires Limited (Supra) is apposite.

entities.text: Ceat Limited Vs. Apollo Tires Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as held in Marico Limited Vs. Abhijit Bhansali (Supra), it becomes amply clear that the goods of the Plaintiff are disparaged if the Defendant's statements are false or that the said statements were made maliciously/ recklessly or that the statements caused special damage to the Plaintiffs.

15. I have seen the Impugned Video which is annexed to the Plaint at Exhibit "H-1" and have perused the storyboard of the Impugned Video along with the translation and transliteration thereof at Exhibit "H-2" to the Plaint.
Prima-facie, I am of the considered opinion that the basic premise of the Impugned Video is to disparage, denigrate and slander the Plaintiff's PITAMBARI product.

Further, in view of the massive reach which the Defendant's video has received (over 2,40,000 views as on 5th August, 2025), it prima facie appears that the Impugned Video is causing irreparable harm, loss and damage to the Plaintiff's PITAMBARI product and the goodwill and reputation acquired by the Plaintiff therein.
16. The Defendant has full freedom to talk about the good aspect of its own product and use exaggerations or simple truth to catch the eyes of the consumer.

However, the Defendant should also exercise caution to ensure that in the said process, it does not ridicule or disrepute the product Pitambari Products Private Limited vs Sawariya Collection Delhi on 14 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122493715/
5 of other parties (such as the Plaintiff herein), 916- IA(L) 25035.2025 in COMIP(L) 24983.2025.doc which, in my prima facie view, the Defendant has done in the present case.
17.

5

sentences.text: In view of the above, applying the well-settled principles of law to the present case and after considering the manner, intent and message conveyed by the Impugned Video, I prima facie find that the Impugned Video denigrates and disparages the Plaintiff's PITAMBARI product.
Further, in view of the averments made in paragraph 30 of the Plaint, I am satisfied that this Court has jurisdiction to entertain and try the present suit filed by the Plaintiff.
18. In the aforesaid circumstances, I am satisfied that the Plaintiff has made out a strong prima facie case for the grant of ad-interim reliefs.
The balance of convenience is in favour of the Plaintiff.
Unless reliefs as prayed for are granted, the Plaintiff will suffer irreparable harm / injury which cannot be compensated in terms of money.

In view of the averments made in paragraph 28 of the Plaint, I am satisfied that giving notice to the Defendants before passing this order would defeat the very purpose of granting ad-interim reliefs.
In the circumstances, there shall be ad-interim relief in terms of prayer clauses (a) and (b) of the Interim Application against the Defendant.
The Plaintiff will comply with the provisions of Order 39 Rule 3 of the CPC.

20. Liberty to the Defendant to apply for a variation, modification or recall of this order after at least 7 clear working days' notice to the Advocates of the Plaintiff.
21.
List the above Interim Application on 8 th September, 2025, for further consideration.
This order shall continue to operate till 9th September, 2025.
22. All concerned will act on production of a digitally signed copy of this order.

[ R. I. CHAGLA, J.]
